note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, session time and indoor-or-outdoor answer below comes from two City of Tampa pages: the pickleball page, a grid of cards dated "Updated: 10/28/2025" that carries a label, a name, an address and a count for every venue, and the recreation-centres list, which gives each community centre an address, a phone number and a "Features:" line. The City's separate tennis page was read too and does not mention pickleball, so nothing on this page rests on it. Where the City stays silent - on lighting, on price, on surface, on hours at most parks - this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking: The City of Tampa publishes nothing about parking at any of the sixteen venues on this page. The word does not appear on the pickleball page, whose cards carry a label, a name, an address and a count and very little else, and the recreation-centres page gives each centre a phone number and a "Features:" line without mentioning a lot. This site does not fill that gap from a map. What the City does publish shapes the trip in other ways. Twelve of the sixteen venues are parks or a pavilion listed under "Outdoor Pickleball", and four are community centres whose courts are inside a building and open only at the session times the City prints - so at Barksdale, Cordelia B Hunt, Loretta Ingraham and Port Tampa the question is not where to leave the car but whether the gym is open at all. The recreation-centres page gives each of those centres a phone number, and for a court the City itself says was "closed for repairs through June 1", the number is worth more than a parking note. For the outdoor parks the addresses are the useful thing, and they are worth reading carefully: the Census geocoder answered four of them by changing or dropping a compass direction, and this site checked each against OpenStreetMap before publishing the address the City prints. Restrooms, like parking, are not mentioned anywhere by the City for these venues.
slots.peak_hours: Tampa states hours for two of its twelve outdoor venues and for the pavilion, and for none of the other nine. Madison Street Park and Vila Brothers Park are "Open daily from sunrise to sunset" on their cards. The New Tampa Sports Pavilion prints facility hours - "Monday-Friday, 4:30-9 pm / Saturday-Sunday, 8 am-9 pm" - the only outdoor hours in the city that run to a clock time rather than to sunset. Cuscaden Park carries the one scheduled outdoor session the City publishes, "Senior open play Wed 9-11 am", a fact about who is on its six courts on a Wednesday morning rather than an hours line. Al Barnes, Copeland, Davis Islands, Forest Hills, Highland Pines, Julian B Lane, Macfarlane and Skyview have no stated hours, and because the City states no lighting for any venue in Tampa, this site cannot say whether evening play is possible at any of them. Indoors the picture reverses: all five indoor venues come with a session schedule, and the sessions are narrow. Barksdale runs weekday afternoons: Monday 1-3 pm with free beginner lessons, then 3-5:30 pm, and Tuesday to Friday 2-5:30 pm. Forest Hills runs Monday 10 am-12:30 pm, Wednesday 10 am-1 pm and Friday 6-7:30 pm. Loretta Ingraham runs Monday and Friday 6:30-8:30 pm until summer camp begins, then Mondays only from June 2. Cordelia B Hunt runs Tuesday and Thursday evenings in two versions split at June 1. Port Tampa runs Tuesday and Thursday 6-9 pm, with a repair closure on the same card. Two cards say "Play resumes after Summer Camp ends" and none of the dates carries a year, on a page the City dates 28 October 2025. Read the schedules as the City's last statement rather than this week's promise, and ring the centre first.
slots.surface_condition: The City names no surface for any pickleball court in Tampa. No card says asphalt, concrete, acrylic or cushioned, and the recreation-centres page describes the buildings - gymnasium, fitness room, computer lab, pool - without describing floors. What the City does distinguish, on every card, is indoor from outdoor. Twelve venues are labelled "Outdoor Pickleball" and the community-centre courts sit under a heading that reads "Indoor Pickleball"; the label and the heading are the City's own words, so every Tampa venue carries an indoor-or-outdoor answer. Beyond that, two outdoor cards say something about what is underfoot. Davis Islands has "2 multi-purpose courts", the City's own word rather than pickleball courts, which means a court that may be lined or set up for something else when you arrive. Julian B Lane Riverfront Park has "2 permanent courts" and "4 portable net courts", so two of its six have nets that are always there and four are laid out for nets that are not. Every other outdoor card just says courts, and this site does not read dedicated into that. Indoors, three of the five venues - Forest Hills, Loretta Ingraham and Port Tampa - list a gymnasium among their features on the recreation-centres page, and Barksdale and Cordelia B Hunt do not; the City says nothing about the floor at any of them. Port Tampa's court was, on the City's page, "closed for repairs through June 1", the only statement about a court's condition anywhere in the city.
slots.local_scene: Fifty-two verified courts across sixteen venues, forty-five of them outdoors and seven inside community-centre buildings, every one counted on a single City page dated 28 October 2025. Macfarlane Park's eight is the largest published set; Cuscaden Park and Julian B Lane Riverfront Park hold six each; five venues hold four; the rest hold one or two. Tampa is the second Florida city on this site after Cape Coral and the first in Hillsborough County, and it is one of the largest cities on this site where the operator states indoor or outdoor for every published venue. It also has more published indoor venues than any city here except Wichita, which is why Tampa has an indoor page, one of only a few on the site. What the City does not state is as much a part of the record as what it does: no lighting for any venue, no price for any court, no surface anywhere, and hours for only two parks and the pavilion. The "free beginner lessons" on Monday afternoons at Barksdale price a lesson, not a court, so no Tampa venue carries a fee answer. Three venues the City lists are not published, and they are named here rather than dropped. Rowlett Park has "8 courts", tied for the largest count in Tampa, at "2401 E Yukon St." - an address neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap can find. Foster Park has two courts at "4700 S Clark Ave., 33611", which the Census geocoder answers as North Clark Avenue in 33614 and OpenStreetMap cannot find as written. The Dr Martin Luther King Jr. Complex has two indoor courts with a schedule the City marks as not yet set and two City house numbers - 220 N Oregon Ave on the pickleball page, 2200 on the recreation-centres page - and the count-bearing one resolves to 33606 while the City prints 33607 on both pages.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts
best_for.text: Macfarlane Park has eight outdoor pickleball courts on the City's card, the largest published set in Tampa - Rowlett Park's eight are not published because its address resolves nowhere. Eight courts is enough for a rotation to form and keep moving, which makes this the venue where turning up without a group is the most reasonable plan. The City states no hours, lighting, price or surface.

best_for.heading: Best if you want a court outside and one under a roof
best_for.text: Forest Hills has two outdoor courts and two indoor courts at one address, 724 W 109th Ave, on two City cards. The indoor pair runs to a schedule - Monday 10 am-12:30 pm, Wednesday 10 am-1 pm, Friday 6-7:30 pm - with "Play resumes after Summer Camp ends" printed beside it. The centre has a gymnasium and a phone number, 813-931-2105, on the City's recreation-centres list.

best_for.heading: Best if you want hours the City has actually written down
best_for.text: The New Tampa Sports Pavilion prints hours on its card - "Monday-Friday, 4:30-9 pm / Saturday-Sunday, 8 am-9 pm" - and no other Tampa outdoor venue gives a closing time later than sunset. Four courts, labelled outdoor by the City, at the same address as the New Tampa Recreation Center, 813-975-2794. Whether the evening hours are lit is not stated; this site does not infer it from the clock.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Tampa have?
faqs.a: We have verified 52 across sixteen City venues: 45 outdoor and 7 indoor. Macfarlane Park has eight, Cuscaden and Julian B Lane six each, five venues have four, and the rest have one or two. The City also lists Rowlett Park with eight courts, Foster Park with two and the Dr Martin Luther King Jr. Complex with two, none of which we can publish.

The City does not say, for any venue. Not one of the sixteen cards mentions lighting, and this site records a lighting answer only when an operator states one, so every Tampa venue is recorded as unverified rather than lit or unlit. The New Tampa Sports Pavilion prints hours to 9 pm, but the City does not write the word lights beside them.

faqs.q: Are there indoor courts in Tampa?
faqs.a: Yes, seven, in five community centres under the City's own "Indoor Pickleball" heading: two at Forest Hills, two at Loretta Ingraham, and one each at Barksdale, Cordelia B Hunt and Port Tampa. Each comes with a session schedule rather than open hours, and Port Tampa's card also says the court was closed for repairs through June 1.

faqs.q: Why is Rowlett Park not listed, when it has eight courts?
faqs.a: Because neither address resolver can find "2401 E Yukon St.": the US Census address file returns no match and OpenStreetMap returns nothing at house-number level. A venue at an address nobody can locate does not publish here. It is the most expensive refusal in Tampa - eight courts, tied with Macfarlane - and it fails on its address alone.

faqs.q: Why are Foster Park and the Dr Martin Luther King Jr. Complex not listed?
faqs.a: Foster Park's "4700 S Clark Ave., 33611" is answered by the Census geocoder as North Clark Avenue in 33614, and OpenStreetMap cannot find it as written, so it has not resolved. The MLK Complex has two City house numbers, 220 and 2200 N Oregon Ave, and the one carrying the count resolves to a postcode the City's own pages contradict.

sources.evidence: The sixteen published addresses were matched at house-number level and placed in Hillsborough County, FL, inside the incorporated place Tampa. Ten resolved through the Census address file as the City writes them. Four resolved through OpenStreetMap: Al Barnes Park and Julian B Lane Riverfront Park because the Census file holds no record of the address, Madison Street Park because the Census dropped the East from "1224 E Madison St", and Cordelia B Hunt Center because the Census answered "4602 N Himes Ave" with "4602 S HIMES AVE, 33611". Highland Pines Park and Skyview Park stand on Census answers that change the City's street type or drop its direction, because OpenStreetMap holds nothing for the address as written. "2401 E Yukon St." (Rowlett Park) is found by neither resolver; "4700 S Clark Ave., 33611" (Foster Park) is answered by the Census as "4700 N CLARK AVE, 33614" and not found by OpenStreetMap; "220 N Oregon Ave." (Dr Martin Luther King Jr. Complex) resolves in 33606 against the City's 33607. Snapshot: data/sources/tampa-county-census.json
